meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on a zero before anyone spoke to my son?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
That wasn't my question. Show me, with the dates.
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
11:52 PM and 11:58 PM. I'm writing that down. Students draft elsewhere and paste it in, so was Owen asked about it before the zero went in?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,
cc: the principal

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that Owen receive an apology, and that I be told who decided on it and whether he was heard first. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Opening position. She agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a visit to the principal. That is not the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4; her time did not run out, the meeting stopped after two exchanges.
What moved her: Nothing yet. Your version history with its two late edit times was the first thing she could check, but she raised her one defence, that students draft elsewhere and paste it in, and the meeting ended before you answered it.
What cost ground: You skipped her opening question about who decided on the zero before Owen was heard and went straight to your evidence, so she got sharper and kept returning to procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your two edits just before midnight came close to that hour, though you gave no date, so she could not place them on any particular night. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether Owen was asked before the zero went in, say in one sentence that it was entered before anyone called home and that this was wrong, then answer her pasting defence with the date of those edits and the screen turned toward her.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
